title: Daemon copy-on-write file clone
scope: Namespace::clone_file, resident fs-clone-file SOURCE TARGET RPC, and offline fs-clone-file CONTAINER SOURCE TARGET CLI
The source final symlink is followed; regular files are cloned, directories return EISDIR, and occupied destinations return EEXIST without publishing namespace changes
A clone has a distinct inode and one link; source mode, supported flags, atime/mtime/birth time, size, representation, sparse content, and xattrs are retained while source metadata remains unchanged
Content and xattr object references are reused without reading payload bytes or iterating logical holes; subsequent file, xattr, and flag edits are inode-independent

C++ modern LevelDB and legacy tests cover empty, inline, chunked and 1 TiB sparse files, symlink/hardlink source resolution, destination and parent errors, source protection, snapshots/forks, reopen, and mutation independence
Modern-only object-ID assertions cover inline and empty content, chunk payloads, and xattrs. Modern handle retention and GC tests close all handles before GC

RPC/offline CLI tests cover clone success, target conflicts, malformed RPC arity, resident mount lease refusal, World selection, and baseline unsupported-command rejection with unchanged namespace state

baseline_probe.status: passed; unsupported RPC and offline CLI commands rejected without namespace state change
baseline_probe.qualification: The baseline C++ Namespace API did not include clone_file, so baseline differential coverage is limited to RPC and offline CLI.

initial_fixture_attempt.status: failed and corrected before final validation
initial_fixture_attempt.cause: The new C++ fixture requested GC while handles were open; the existing GC policy requires an idle offline repository.
initial_fixture_attempt.correction: The fixture now reads and closes all handles before requesting GC. Runtime code and GC policy were not changed.

explicit_exclusions: No FSKit callback, native clonefile(2)/copyfile(3) clone capability, or mounted clone behavior is implemented or claimed.
No physical disk deduplication/space guarantee or performance benchmark is established; the 1 TiB sparse case is a bounded regression, not a benchmark.
Reference-ID equality is asserted on the modern backend only; legacy tests validate clone behavior but do not assert object-ID equality.
Modern handle-retention and GC coverage is modern-only, and GC is requested only after all handles are closed.
The focused tests do not assert the newly created inode change-time value or explicitly test a destination that is a hardlink to the source.
Baseline differential coverage is resident RPC and offline CLI only because the baseline C++ Namespace API did not include clone_file.
